On an input orthant |a_i|=s_i*a_i; each output root oscillation is the maximum of explicit linear target forms. I independently reconstructed the 290 distinct nonzero input rows and, using exact BigInt rational arithmetic rather than trusting a verifier success string, checked every one of the 910 frozen certificate.json dual coordinate identities, 4,739 positive rational weights, the upper sum-of-row-coefficients bound <=1 and nonnegative orthant penalties, with no failure; maximum coefficient mass is exactly 1. Independent generation of 128 rooted-tree automorphisms, 13 sign classes up to simultaneous sign inversion, and canonical stabilizer orbits proved the provided 910 cases exactly exhaust all nontrivial sign-cell/target-subset possibilities. These finite polyhedral certificates are a complete inequality proof for all real eight-leaf vectors, not a finite input experiment. The two- and four-atom folding bound handles proper descendant nodes; the source cites Mohajer for this prior lemma. Exact computation of the 16-leaf witness yielded input seminorm 5, output 41/8, so the first amplification depth is exactly 4. The conclusion is only for real equal-weight mean-centered binary-tree BMO; it does not give the optimal depth-four constant.
